subject: I-O status
notes: kb/Work PB328, LANDED (the write halves; item 6 b) was kb/Work PB323 and item 6 a) 3. is measured here for the first time). RULE: I-O status = 37 for four distinct reasons, each checked separately. 6) a) 1. (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the EXTEND or OUTPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support write operations': OK, 6) a) 1.) -- CONFORMS since PB328: FileConnector.Open asks HostFile.PermitsWrite for EXTEND and OUTPUT on a Present file before OpenCore. Measured on a worktree build at 17c11fd4 with three compiler-created files made read-only: BEFORE, OPEN EXTEND answered SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' (the relative and indexed EXTEND arms only Attach(), so nothing probed writability) and the keyed WRITE that followed reported '00' before CLOSE lost it as '30'; AFTER, 37/37/37. OPEN OUTPUT was already 37/37/37 because the keyed OUTPUT arm eagerly calls RecordFraming.WriteStore. 6) a) 2. (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the I-O phrase is specified but the file will not support the input and output operations that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode': OK, 6) a) 2.) -- the status-side statement of 14.9.27.4 16); see GR-14.9.27.4-16 for the full forensic record. Measured BEFORE: SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00'; AFTER: 37/37/37. 6) a) 3. (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the INPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support read operations': OK, 6) a) 3.) -- CONFORMS, and now MEASURED rather than assumed: the answer is neither the write probe (INPUT is deliberately outside it) nor GR3's presence short-circuit, because the file here is fully observable -- only the FILE is denied read while its directory stays listable, so File.GetAttributes succeeds and HostFile.Probe answers Present. It is the organization's own eager read -- the sequential StreamReader, the keyed Attach() -- whose UnauthorizedAccessException reaches '37' through FileConnector.Open's catch. Probed on a worktree build with icacls /deny :(R) on the data files themselves: OPEN INPUT answered '37' on sequential, relative and indexed, with GetAttributes succeeding on all three (so the presence probe was NOT the producer). This sub-case had been the unexamined premise of PB328's INPUT exclusion; it is asserted now because an exclusion resting on an unmeasured claim is how a gap ships. 6) b) (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'insufficient authority exists to access the file': OK, 6) b)) -- CONFORMS since kb/Work PB323: the three-state HostFile.Probe distinguishes an absent file from a present-but-unobservable one, FileConnector.Open answers 14.9.27.4 3) from it for INPUT/I-O/EXTEND, and FileRegistry.DeleteFile takes the same probe for 14.9.10.4 GR14/GR16. The clause's own caveat -- 'The ability to detect this is processor dependent' -- is honoured rather than leaned on: every arm detects. OVER-FIRE MEASURED for each producer: a read-only file still OPENs INPUT '00' on all three organizations, a writable file still opens I-O '00', and a NEW file under a directory this process may write but not list still opens OUTPUT '00' (14.9.27.4 18) makes OUTPUT a creation that never consults presence). COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes every precondition for real -- a read-only attribute or mode 0400 for the write cases, a DACL deny ACE or mode 000 for the observation cases, a file-level deny-read for 6) a) 3. -- and verifies each with a raw stream open rather than with the subject under test; on a host that cannot deny anything to this process the class asserts POSITIVELY that this process is permission-bypassing, so a broken helper goes red instead of vacuously green. No conformance golden can reach any of these arms: the corpus runner compiles a .cob and compares its output, with nowhere to express the precondition. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 -- the '37' family is emitted at every edition and not gated (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3; Annex E.2 item 18 is a clarification that '37' is allowed, not a 2023 introduction).
